items.title: Pointed! Bloomberg's Weekly News Quiz For Risk-Takers
items.content: Pointed offers a strategic twist to the news quiz format, testing not just players’ knowledge of the news but also their confidence in their answers. Join Bloomberg's Alexis Christoforous, Christina Ruffini and David Gura as they play and check out the quiz for yourself at Bloomberg.com (Source: Bloomberg)

items.title: Trump-Xi Summit Yields Coal Pledge as Tariff Talks Extend
items.content: China agreed to import at least 10 million metric tons of coal from the US next year and again in 2028, according to the White House, in a sign of progress in easing trade frictions.
items.contentSnippet: China agreed to import at least 10 million metric tons of coal from the US next year and again in 2028, according to the White House, in a sign of progress in easing trade frictions.
items.creator: Bloomberg News

summaries.zh: 白宫表示，中国同意在2027年和2028年分别从美国进口至少1000万吨煤炭，这标志着中美两大经济体贸易摩擦进一步缓和。
summaries.en: The White House reports that China has agreed to import at least 10 million metric tons of coal from the US in 2027 and 2028. This agreement is seen as a sign of progress in easing trade tensions between the world’s two largest economies.

items.title: US and China Seek Common Ground on AI
items.content: Bloomberg News Chief North Asia Correspondent Stephen Engle and ABC News State Department reporter Shannon Kingston tell Bloomberg This Weekend that President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping’s summit highlighted efforts to establish dialogue on AI while building trust between the two countries. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Engle and Kingston examine the significance of Xi’s state visit, China’s push to be treated as an equal to the US and the diplomatic signals surrounding the meetings. (Source: Bloomberg)
items.contentSnippet: Bloomberg News Chief North Asia Correspondent Stephen Engle and ABC News State Department reporter Shannon Kingston tell Bloomberg This Weekend that President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping’s summit highlighted efforts to establish dialogue on AI while building trust between the two countries. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Engle and Kingston examine the significance of Xi’s state visit, China’s push to be treated as an equal to the US and the diplomatic signals surrounding the meetings. (Source: Bloomberg)

summaries.zh: 美中两国在人工智能领域寻求共识。彭博社北亚首席记者Stephen Engle和ABC新闻国务院记者Shannon Kingston表示，特朗普与习近平峰会强调了建立人工智能对话和增进两国互信的努力。他们还探讨了习近平国事访问的意义、中国寻求被视为美国平等伙伴以及会议中的外交信号。（来源：彭博）
summaries.en: The summit between President Trump and President Xi Jinping emphasized efforts to establish dialogue on AI and build trust between the US and China. Bloomberg's Stephen Engle and ABC News' Shannon Kingston discussed the significance of Xi's state visit, China's desire for equal treatment, and diplomatic signals during the meetings. The discussions aimed to foster cooperation in AI while addressing broader diplomatic relations. (Word count: 50)

items.title: How Syracuse's Semiconductor Gamble May Help Save the Rust Belt
items.content: What does it actually take to bring a Rust Belt city back to life? Micron is building one of the largest semiconductor factories in US history in Syracuse, a city that experienced major job loss after companies including GE, Carrier and General Motors left the area. Rob Simpson of CenterState CEO explains what attracted Micron to the city, local business owner Darin Price talks about what the investment means on the ground, and Brookings economist Joseph Parilla makes the case that Syracuse could be a model for reindustrialization across America. (Source: Bloomberg)

Micron is building one of the largest semiconductor factories in US history in Syracuse, a city that experienced major job loss after companies including GE, Carrier and General Motors left the area. summaries.en: Micron is constructing a massive semiconductor factory in Syracuse, a city struggling with job losses after GE, Carrier, and General Motors left. Local leaders highlight the investment's potential to revitalize the Rust Belt. Analysts suggest Syracuse could serve as a model for national reindustrialization. The project aims to boost the city's economy and create high-tech employment opportunities.

items.title: Birding Apps Bring More People Into the Wild
items.content: On Bloomberg This Weekend, writer and photographer Alexandra Marvar explains how apps such as Merlin are making birding easier and more accessible, helping draw new people to a hobby that offers an escape into nature. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Marvar also explores whether technology can remove some of the challenge, learning and satisfaction that traditionally come with identifying birds.  (Source: Bloomberg)
items.contentSnippet: On Bloomberg This Weekend, writer and photographer Alexandra Marvar explains how apps such as Merlin are making birding easier and more accessible, helping draw new people to a hobby that offers an escape into nature. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Marvar also explores whether technology can remove some of the challenge, learning and satisfaction that traditionally come with identifying birds.  (Source: Bloomberg)

summaries.zh: 《彭博》节目报道了作家兼摄影师亚历山德拉·马尔瓦的观点。她指出，如Merlin等观鸟应用简化了观鸟过程，提升了可及性，吸引更多人参与这项亲近自然的活动。马尔瓦还探讨了科技是否削弱了传统观鸟的挑战、学习与成就感。
summaries.en: Birding apps like Merlin are making birding more accessible by simplifying identification, attracting newcomers to the hobby. Writer Alexandra Marvar discusses this trend on Bloomberg, noting how apps provide an escape into nature. She also explores whether technology diminishes the traditional challenges, learning, and satisfaction of birding. The discussion centers on the impact of apps on both accessibility and the core experience of birdwatching.

items.title: Mexico Stresses Sovereignty in US Cooperation
items.content: Mexico’s foreign minister Roberto Velasco Álvarez tells Bloomberg This Weekend that the country maintains a strong relationship with the US while insisting cooperation on security must respect Mexico’s sovereignty and territorial integrity. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, he says Mexico remains cautiously optimistic about ongoing trade negotiations as it seeks relief from US tariffs on automobiles and steel. (Source: Bloomberg)
items.contentSnippet: Mexico’s foreign minister Roberto Velasco Álvarez tells Bloomberg This Weekend that the country maintains a strong relationship with the US while insisting cooperation on security must respect Mexico’s sovereignty and territorial integrity. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, he says Mexico remains cautiously optimistic about ongoing trade negotiations as it seeks relief from US tariffs on automobiles and steel. (Source: Bloomberg)

summaries.zh: 墨西哥外长罗伯托·韦拉斯科·阿尔瓦雷斯表示，墨西哥与美国保持密切关系，但强调安全合作必须尊重墨西哥的主权和领土完整。他对正在进行的贸易谈判持谨慎乐观态度，希望缓解美国对汽车和钢铁征收的关税。来源：彭博社。
summaries.en: Mexico’s foreign minister, Roberto Velasco Álvarez, emphasized sovereignty and territorial integrity in US cooperation, particularly on security matters, while maintaining a strong relationship with the US. He expressed cautious optimism about ongoing trade negotiations, seeking relief from US tariffs on automobiles and steel. (Source: Bloomberg)

items.title: Russia Ukraine War Becomes Economic Battle
items.content: New York Times Kyiv bureau chief Andrew Kramer tells Bloomberg This Weekend that Russia and Ukraine are increasingly targeting each other’s economies as the war shifts toward attacks on energy, transportation and export infrastructure. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Kramer says Ukraine is using its expanding drone arsenal to target Russia’s oil industry and its ability to finance a prolonged war. (Source: Bloomberg)
items.contentSnippet: New York Times Kyiv bureau chief Andrew Kramer tells Bloomberg This Weekend that Russia and Ukraine are increasingly targeting each other’s economies as the war shifts toward attacks on energy, transportation and export infrastructure. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Kramer says Ukraine is using its expanding drone arsenal to target Russia’s oil industry and its ability to finance a prolonged war. (Source: Bloomberg)

summaries.zh: 俄乌战争正演变为经济战。据《纽约时报》基辅分社首席记者安德鲁·克莱默向彭博社表示，双方越来越多地针对彼此经济，通过攻击能源、交通和出口基础设施。克莱默指出，乌克兰正利用其不断扩大的无人机库，打击俄罗斯的石油产业及其长期战争融资能力。
summaries.en: The Russia-Ukraine war is escalating into an economic battle, with both sides targeting energy, transportation, and export infrastructure. Ukraine is using its drone arsenal to strike Russia's oil industry and hinder its financial capabilities for a prolonged conflict. This shift reflects the war's growing economic dimensions, as outlined by New York Times bureau chief Andrew Kramer in a Bloomberg interview.

items.title: McDonald’s Selloff Hits 30% as Big Mac Inflation Spurs Pushback
items.content: McDonald’s Corp. faces a key challenge as it fights to reinvigorate a sagging stock price: Winning back the cost-conscious diners who believe its menu has become too expensive.
items.contentSnippet: McDonald’s Corp. faces a key challenge as it fights to reinvigorate a sagging stock price: Winning back the cost-conscious diners who believe its menu has become too expensive.
items.creator: Peyton Forte

summaries.zh: 麦当劳股价面临挑战，因高通胀导致消费者对其菜单价格不满。公司需吸引注重性价比的顾客，以提振低迷的股价。
summaries.en: McDonald's Corp. is experiencing a 30% stock price decline due to rising menu costs, particularly the Big Mac, which has led to consumer pushback. The company struggles to regain the trust of cost-conscious customers who find its offerings too expensive.

items.title: Higher Bond Yields Mark a Return to Normal
items.content: Ritholtz Wealth Management founder Barry Ritholtz tells Bloomberg This Weekend that rising bond yields reflect both a normalization of interest rates and inflationary pressures from factors including tariffs and higher energy prices. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Ritholtz says higher yields have made fixed income more attractive while investors should consider whether strong equity gains have pushed their portfolios away from their intended allocations. (Source: Bloomberg)
items.contentSnippet: Ritholtz Wealth Management founder Barry Ritholtz tells Bloomberg This Weekend that rising bond yields reflect both a normalization of interest rates and inflationary pressures from factors including tariffs and higher energy prices. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Ritholtz says higher yields have made fixed income more attractive while investors should consider whether strong equity gains have pushed their portfolios away from their intended allocations. (Source: Bloomberg)

summaries.zh: 债券收益率上升标志着回归常态。Ritholtz Wealth Management创始人Barry Ritholtz表示，这一现象反映了利率正常化和关税、能源价格上涨等导致的通胀压力。他认为，高收益率使固定收益更具吸引力，同时建议投资者评估股价上涨是否导致其投资组合偏离了预定配置。来源：彭博社。
summaries.en: Higher bond yields indicate a return to normalcy, reflecting interest rate normalization and inflationary pressures from tariffs and rising energy costs, according to Barry Ritholtz of Ritholtz Wealth Management. He notes that elevated yields make fixed income more appealing and advises investors to assess whether strong equity gains have shifted portfolio allocations from their intended targets. (Source: Bloomberg)

items.title: Northeast Faces Wind, Rain and Coastal Flooding
items.content: Bloomberg News meteorologist Craig Allen tells Bloomberg This Weekend that the nor'easter will bring waves of heavy rain and strong winds to the Northeast, along with risks from falling trees, localized flooding and dangerous coastal conditions. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Allen says coastal flooding could affect Long Island, the Jersey Shore, Connecticut and Massachusetts as rough ocean conditions persist through multiple high-tide cycles. (Source: Bloomberg)
items.contentSnippet: Bloomberg News meteorologist Craig Allen tells Bloomberg This Weekend that the nor'easter will bring waves of heavy rain and strong winds to the Northeast, along with risks from falling trees, localized flooding and dangerous coastal conditions. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Allen says coastal flooding could affect Long Island, the Jersey Shore, Connecticut and Massachusetts as rough ocean conditions persist through multiple high-tide cycles. (Source: Bloomberg)

summaries.zh: 东北将面临大风、暴雨和沿海洪水。气象学家克雷格·艾伦表示，此次东北风暴将带来强风和暴雨，可能导致树木倒塌、局部洪水和危险的沿海条件。沿海洪水可能影响长岛、新泽西海岸、康涅狄格州和马萨诸塞州，因恶劣海况将持续多个高潮周期。
summaries.en: The Northeast is experiencing a nor'easter, bringing heavy rain, strong winds, and coastal flooding. Meteorologist Craig Allen warns of risks including falling trees, localized flooding, and dangerous coastal conditions. Coastal flooding may affect Long Island, the Jersey Shore, Connecticut, and Massachusetts due to rough ocean conditions during high tides. (Source: Bloomberg)

items.title: Iran War Endgame Remains Elusive
items.content: Bloomberg Mideast geoeconomics lead Dina Esfandiary tells Bloomberg This Weekend that a protracted Iran war, marked by cycles of escalation and pauses in fighting, is a key scenario as deep divisions over the Strait of Hormuz complicate diplomacy. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Esfandiary says Gulf Arab states are pressing to avoid further escalation as they seek to limit the economic and security damage from the conflict.  (Source: Bloomberg)
items.contentSnippet: Bloomberg Mideast geoeconomics lead Dina Esfandiary tells Bloomberg This Weekend that a protracted Iran war, marked by cycles of escalation and pauses in fighting, is a key scenario as deep divisions over the Strait of Hormuz complicate diplomacy. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Esfandiary says Gulf Arab states are pressing to avoid further escalation as they seek to limit the economic and security damage from the conflict. summaries.zh: 伊朗战争以周期性升级和停火为特征，前景不明。深陷霍尔木兹海峡分歧的冲突导致外交复杂化。海湾阿拉伯国家正努力避免进一步升级，以减少经济和安全损失。据彭博报道，彭博中东地缘经济首席分析师丁娜·埃斯凡迪里表示，长期战争是关键场景。
summaries.en: A protracted Iran war, characterized by cycles of escalation and pauses, is a key scenario as deep divisions over the Strait of Hormuz complicate diplomacy, according to Bloomberg's Dina Esfandiary. Gulf Arab states are pressing to avoid further escalation to limit economic and security damage from the conflict.

items.title: The China Trade Problem That Tariffs Alone Can't Fix
items.content: China ran a $1.2 trillion trade surplus last year, many of its companies don't need to make a profit, and its exports are growing at two to three times the rate of the global economy. Michael Froman, former US Trade Representative under President Obama and now president of the Council on Foreign Relations, tells us why Xi Jinping sees a consumer-led economy as a political threat, and what happens when China finally runs out of countries willing to buy. (Source: Bloomberg)
items.contentSnippet: China ran a $1.2 trillion trade surplus last year, many of its companies don't need to make a profit, and its exports are growing at two to three times the rate of the global economy. Michael Froman, former US Trade Representative under President Obama and now president of the Council on Foreign Relations, tells us why Xi Jinping sees a consumer-led economy as a political threat, and what happens when China finally runs out of countries willing to buy. (Source: Bloomberg)

summaries.zh: 去年中国贸易顺差达1.2万亿美元，许多企业无需盈利，出口增速是全球经济的两到三倍。前美国贸易代表迈克尔·弗里德曼（现为美国外交关系委员会主席）指出，习近平将消费型经济视为政治威胁，并警示中国终将耗尽购买国。
summaries.en: China's $1.2 trillion trade surplus highlights its export-driven growth, outpacing the global economy at 2-3 times the rate. Many Chinese companies operate without profit needs. Former US Trade Representative Michael Froman suggests President Xi Jinping views a consumer-led economy as politically risky. Concerns arise as China exhausts willing international buyers. Tariffs alone cannot resolve this trade imbalance.

items.title: Trump Xi Summit Leaves Big Issues Unresolved
items.content: Bloomberg North Asia correspondent Stephen Engle tells Bloomberg This Weekend that President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping bought more time to negotiate over trade while major disagreements involving Taiwan, Iran and technology remain. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Engle explains how competition over AI and unresolved economic and security issues are shaping the next phase of US-China relations. (Source: Bloomberg)
items.contentSnippet: Bloomberg North Asia correspondent Stephen Engle tells Bloomberg This Weekend that President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping bought more time to negotiate over trade while major disagreements involving Taiwan, Iran and technology remain. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Engle explains how competition over AI and unresolved economic and security issues are shaping the next phase of US-China relations. (Source: Bloomberg)

summaries.zh: 特朗普与习近平峰会未能解决重大分歧。据彭博报道，此次会晤为贸易谈判争取了时间，但台湾、伊朗和技术等关键问题仍悬而未决。人工智能竞争及未解决的经济与安全问题将影响中美关系的下一阶段。
summaries.en: The Trump-Xi summit extended negotiation time on trade but left major issues unresolved, including disagreements over Taiwan, Iran, and technology. According to Bloomberg's Stephen Engle, competition in AI and unresolved economic and security matters will influence the next phase of US-China relations.

items.title: Wall Street Week | China’s Trade Reckoning, Syracuse’s Second Chance, Humanoids in Healthcare
items.content: This week, Council on Foreign Relations President Michael Froman breaks down China's export machine, why twenty years of US pressure hasn't worked, and what happens next. And, can a $100 billion Micron factory transform Syracuse from a Rust Belt cautionary tale into a potential model for American reindustrialization? Plus, a bridge named for a hockey legend was meant to strengthen the supply chain between the US and Canada, but the neighbors can’t agree on their trade relationship. Later, with 760,000 care aide openings expected every year in the US and a $400 billion long-term care bill, humanoid robots are an early bet on technology filling the care gap. (Source: Bloomberg)

The pledge is a standard practice for executives securing loans against company shares.

items.title: David Booth on Investing, Dimensional and Staying Calm | The David Rubenstein Show
items.content: David Booth started Dimensional Fund Advisors out of a Brooklyn brownstone in 1981 with an idea that challenged conventional investing: investors should have exposure to smaller companies as part of a diversified portfolio. Today, Dimensional manages more than $1 trillion. Booth sits down with David Rubenstein to discuss his new book, "Stay Calm," which applies his investment philosophy of staying calm during periods of market volatility, to navigating the uncertainties of life. He's on this week's episode of The David Rubenstein Show: Peer to Peer Conversations. This interview was recorded August 10 in New York. (Source: Bloomberg)

summaries.zh: 大卫·布斯在1981年以布鲁克林一栋棕榈公寓为起点创办了Dimensional Fund Advisors，其投资理念挑战传统，主张投资者应将小盘股纳入多元化投资组合。如今，Dimensional管理资产超1万亿美元。在《大卫·鲁本斯坦秀》中，布斯与主持人讨论新书《保持冷静》，分享其投资哲学：在市场波动和人生不确定性中保持冷静。访谈于8月10日在纽约录制。
